title: Trauma & burns
objectives: Run the paediatric primary survey with weight-based doses and tube sizes.
Apply FAST, CT selective imaging and non-operative solid-organ protocols.
Calculate burns fluids and state escharotomy and referral triggers.
body_md:
### Why this area matters

Trauma questions are ATLS in small bodies plus three paediatric twists: non-operative solid-organ management, SCIWORA, and burns resuscitation. Scores (PTS, ISS, paediatric GCS) are pure recall — memorise every component.

### The paediatric primary survey

Airway with cervical-spine protection first (children desaturate fast), breathing with age-appropriate rates, circulation with weight-based boluses and blood, disability by paediatric GCS (eye/verbal/motor adapted for preverbal children), exposure with warm chain. Tube sizes, IV gauges and drug doses by weight or Broselow thinking belong in the answer, not assumed.

### Blunt trauma and scores

FAST finds free fluid; stable children with solid-organ injury go non-operative with bed rest grading, transfusion thresholds and activity restriction timelines — operation for instability, hollow-viscus injury or pancreatic ductal injury. Paediatric Trauma Score triages, Injury Severity Score squares the three worst AIS regions, paediatric GCS quantifies coma: write components and ranges, not just expansions. SCIWORA reminds you that a normal X-ray never clears a child's cord injury clinically.

### Burns and compartments

Depth and TBSA (Lund-Browder, not adult rule-of-nines for small children) drive Parkland-style resuscitation with urine-output targets; inhalation injury, circumferential eschar and compartment syndrome force escharotomy/fasciotomy decisions. Referral criteria, tetanus, nutrition and staged grafting complete the answer.

### How it is asked

Scenario → survey sequence → score calculation → disposition. Burns add a fluid-maths sub-part — show the formula, the numbers and the endpoints.
